title: Oncall quickcards — compact runbook for inference observability
body:
Purpose
Quick, actionable cheat sheet for oncall engineers investigating inference incidents (latency spikes, token-cost surges, cold-cache regressions, noisy tenants). Compact = < 2 screens. Emphasize: first capture, then escalate.

Scope
- Applies to hosted API + dedicated pools + private control-plane traces.
- Focus: production token-serving paths (request->router->model-proxy->runtime).
- Not in scope: long-running batch jobs, offline eval infra.

Fast triage (first 6 minutes)
1) Capture the incident window and customer scope
   - When did alerts start? = alert.start_ts or slack thread timestamp
   - Which model(s)/route(s)/tenant(s) affected? Check error/latency panels for spikes per-route.
2) Confirm global vs tenant-local
   - Global: many tenants, likely infra or rollout.
   - Tenant-local: single tenant patterns (cold-cache, request spikes).
3) Look at 3 quick panels (ordered)
   - Overall 95p request latency (1m, 5m) by model_variant (panel: request_latency_95p_by_model).
   - Error rate (500/5xx) and throttles by route (panel: request_error_rate_per_route).
   - KV cache hit ratio (1m) and cold-cache churn (panel: kv_cache_hit_ratio).
4) If latency high, open a representative trace from top slow requests (trace links in panel).
5) Annotate incident with suspected cause and escalate to runtime team if 95p > SLO + 50ms and traces show kernel saturation or queued requests.

Metric & SLI definitions (quick canonical list)
- request.latency_p95 (ms) — 95th percentile of end-to-end request latency sampled over window=5m, grouping: model, route, tenant. SLO example: p95 < 300ms for hosted-tier; p95 < 150ms for dedicated-tier (configurable).
- request.error_rate — count(status >=500) / count(requests) over 5m, tag by route/model. Alert: >0.5% sustained over 5m.
- token.cost_per_request — raw_token_cost_usd average per request 1h rolling. Use for cost-surges.
- kv_cache.hit_ratio — hits / (hits + misses) per model-shard over 1m. Cold-cache triggers: drop < 60% with sustained misses.
- gpu.utilization_pct — per node, 1m avg. If >92% with rising queue_length, consider autoscale/burst.
- queue.length_by_shard — pending inference requests waiting for GPU scheduling.

Trace naming & anchors (for fast trace hunting)
- span.service: router, model-proxy, runtime-infer, kernel-compile, cache-lookup
- span.operation examples: route.resolve, request.serialize, kv.lookup, batch.enqueue, model.forward, model.kv_restore, model.kv_flush, kernel.exec
- Anchor spans: kernel.exec (long time = kernel issue), batch.enqueue (queuing/backpressure), kv.lookup (cache-related delays).
- Use trace tags: tenant_id, model_variant, route_id, seq_len, batch_size — these are critical to correlate token-length and batching behaviour.

Dashboards (2-screen minimal layout)
Screen A — Rapid triage (operator view)
  - Panel 1: p95/p50/p99 request latency by model_variant (1m, 5m) — intent: spot regressions and variance.
  - Panel 2: error rate by route and status code — intent: identify code-path failures.
  - Panel 3: top slow traces (click to open) — intent: jump to span-level diagnostics.
  - Panel 4: KV cache hit ratio + miss hotspots (tenant/model) — intent: find cold starts.
  - Panel 5: GPU utilization + queue length heatmap by zone/pool — intent: capacity saturation.
Screen B — Cost & degradation lens (ops view)
  - Panel 1: token cost per 1k requests by model_variant (1h) — intent: detect cost anomalies.
  - Panel 2: batch size distribution and effective token throughput — intent: check batching efficiency.
  - Panel 3: prefix-cache effective hit rate (per-tenant sample) — intent: catch KV regression.
  - Panel 4: fallback routing ratio (requests routed to cheaper fallback model) — intent: verify graceful degradation.

Sampling & trace budget heuristics (cost-aware)
- Default adaptive sampling: 1% baseline traces + structured amplification: sample 100% of all traces that meet any of: latency > p95, error status, cache miss + sequence_len > 512, fallback used.
- Severity-weighted reservoir: keep higher retention for errors and high-cost requests (token length > 1000).
- Spot-check policy: synthetic probes every 5m per region/model_variant (low-cost tokenized prompts) to validate tail latency; if probe fails, increase trace sampling for that model by 10x for 30m.

Investigation quickcards (copy/paste queries)
- Find tenants with highest p95 spike
  SQL-like: SELECT tenant_id, percentile(latency_ms,95) AS p95 FROM requests WHERE timestamp >= now() - interval '15m' GROUP BY tenant_id ORDER BY p95 DESC LIMIT 10;
- Top traces for long kernel.exec spans
  query: traces where span.name = 'kernel.exec' AND span.duration_ms > 200 ORDER BY span.duration_ms DESC LIMIT 20;
- KV churn by model shard
  SELECT model_shard, sum(kv_miss) / sum(kv_hit + kv_miss) AS miss_rate FROM kv_metrics WHERE window='5m' GROUP BY model_shard ORDER BY miss_rate DESC LIMIT 20;

Playbook snippets (short decisions)
- If p95 high + GPU util high + queue rising -> scale: trigger autoscale policy OR move high-volume tenants to dedicated pool; contact infra oncall if autoscale doesn't react in 2m.
- If p95 high + gpu util low + kernel.exec long -> suspect kernel/compilation path: mark rollout, revert last model-variant push, open a kernel debug ticket and attach 3 traces.
- If error_rate spike concentrated on one route and begins with serialization errors -> check router config/dependency (protobuf, schema changes).

Synthetic probes alignment
- Keep probes lightweight: 3 short prompts that exercise prefix cache, KV restore, and long-seq path. Probe cadence: 5m (per prod region), 1m for dedicated customer test routes during initial rollout.
- Probe response validation: expected token counts + latency bounds; failed probes should tag traces and raise a low-severity alert (pager on escalation thresholds).

Open questions / TODOs
- Add automated rerun for sample failing probes to rule out transient infra blips (task: OBS-544).
- Standardize token-cost attribution across dashboards (billing vs per-route counters currently diverge). Owner: Ethan.
- Explore increasing p95 windows for hosts with bursty traffic to avoid noisy alerts.

Notes to self (informal)
- Keep this doc <2 screens; expand each quickcard into full playbook pages later.
- Tie in with product rollout notebook so new model variants automatically generate a mini-observability checklist.

Contact list for escalation
- runtime: @sofia (Sofia Chen) Slack: #runtime-oncall
- infra autoscale: @liam (Liam O'Connor) Slack: #infra-oncall
- obs owners: @maya (Maya Patel) Slack: #observability

End — keep a short changelog in the top comments when updating (date, short note).
